title: श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता — ज्ञानकर्मसंन्यासयोगः
titleEn: The Bhagavad Gītā — Chapter 4: Knowledge, Action and Renunciation
draftNote: Prepared by the Lectorium pipeline from the vulgate text, with a drafting pass, a reviewing pass and a mechanical gate; a printed-edition collation and audio are still to come. Use ⚑ correction on any verse to report a problem.
source: Text: the received (vulgate) text of the Bhagavadgītā, Mahābhārata 6.23–40, as read by Śaṅkara's commentary. Devanagari from Sanskrit Wikisource (भगवद्गीता/ज्ञानकर्मसंन्यासयोगः), collated verse by verse against the GRETIL romanized text based on the BORI critical edition (input Tokunaga, rev. J. Smith); every verse where the two differ carries a note giving the BORI reading, and every correction to the Wikisource text is named in its note. Collation against a pre-1930 printed edition is still to be done. Transliteration: IAST. The reading under each word gives the words with sandhi undone and compound members hyphenated, in the manner of the traditional pada-pāṭha. Pronunciation convention: classical Sanskrit as described in Whitney's Sanskrit Grammar (1889); no audio yet. Translations made fresh from the Sanskrit with Monier-Williams (1899), Apte (1890) and Śaṅkara's commentary for the traditional sense; no modern translation consulted.

विवस्वान्मनवे प्राह मनुरिक्ष्वाकवेऽब्रवीत् ॥
sentences.tr:
imam vivasvate yogam proktavān aham avyayam |
vivasvān manave prāha manuḥ ikṣvākave abravīt ||

morph.gloss: this (acc. sg. masc., referring to yogam)
the sun-god (dat. sg. 'to Vivasvat')

to declare, teach (proktavān: perfect active participle used as a finite verb, 'I have declared, taught')

sentences.l: This imperishable yoga to-Vivasvat I-declared; Vivasvat to-Manu told [it]; Manu to-Ikṣvāku said [it].
sentences.i: I taught this imperishable yoga to Vivasvat; Vivasvat told it to Manu; Manu told it to Ikṣvāku.
sentences.n: A chain of transmission opens the chapter: Vivasvat, the sun-god, to his son Manu (the first man and lawgiver), to Manu's son Ikṣvāku (first king of the solar dynasty, ancestor of Rāma). Proktavān, a perfect participle standing in for a finite verb ('I have declared, taught'), is a common Epic construction for the first person perfect. The claim of vast antiquity here sets up Arjuna's puzzled objection in verse 4 and Kṛṣṇa's answer about his own repeated births in verse 5.

sentences.l: Thus, through-succession-attained, this the-royal-sages knew; that, by-great time here, yoga lost [became], O scorcher-of-the-foe.
sentences.i: Handed down in this succession, the royal sages knew this yoga; but with the passing of great time it was lost here, scorcher of the foe.
sentences.n: Paramparā-prāptam, 'received through an unbroken succession', describes how the yoga in verse 1 continued to be known — by rājarṣayaḥ, 'royal sages' (kings who were also seers, like Ikṣvāku's line, and Janaka at 3.20). Kālena mahatā, 'through great time', explains why Kṛṣṇa must now teach it again: not a new doctrine, but a recovery of one that had lapsed.

sentences.l: That very-same, by-me, to-you today, yoga [has been] declared, ancient — for devoted you-are to-me, [and my] friend; a-secret, indeed, this, supreme.
sentences.i: That very same ancient yoga I have now declared to you, because you are my devotee and my friend; for this is a supreme secret.
sentences.n: Sa eva ayam, 'that very same one', insists this is the identical ancient teaching of verses 1-2, not something newly invented for Arjuna's benefit. Bhakto 'si me sakhā ca, 'you are my devotee and my friend', gives the reason Arjuna specifically receives it: devotion and friendship together, not merit or birth. Rahasyam ... uttamam, 'a supreme secret', is neuter, referring to the teaching itself.

अपरं भवतो जन्म परं जन्म विवस्वतः ।
कथमेतद्विजानीयां त्वमादौ प्रोक्तवानिति ॥

aparam bhavataḥ janma param janma vivasvataḥ |
katham etat vijānīyām tvam ādau proktavān iti ||

sentences.l: Later [is] your birth; earlier, the-birth of-Vivasvat. How this might-I-understand: 'you at-the-beginning declared [it]' — thus [you say]?
sentences.i: Your birth was later, and Vivasvat's birth was earlier. How am I to understand this — that you taught it at the very beginning?
sentences.n: Apara and para here mean 'later' and 'earlier' respectively, a temporal sense of para distinct from its more usual 'higher, supreme'; Śaṅkara glosses aparam as arvācīnam ('recent') and param as pūrvam ('prior'). Arjuna's objection is simple chronology: Kṛṣṇa, born in his own generation, could not literally have taught the sun-god at the dawn of the solar line — setting up the doctrine of verse 5.

तान्यहं वेद सर्वाणि न त्वं वेत्थ परन्तप ॥

sentences.l: Many, of-mine, have-passed, births, and of-yours, O Arjuna; those I know all; not you know, O scorcher-of-the-foe.
sentences.i: Many births of mine have passed, Arjuna, and yours as well; I know them all, but you do not, scorcher of the foe.
sentences.n: Kṛṣṇa's answer to verse 4: rebirth is not in dispute — both he and Arjuna have had bahūni janmāni, 'many births' — the difference is that Kṛṣṇa vetti sarvāṇi, 'knows them all', while ordinary beings like Arjuna do not (na tvaṃ vettha). This unbroken divine memory, not a denial of prior existence, is what makes the claim of verse 1 possible, and it leads directly into verse 6's account of how such births occur at all.

प्रकृतिं स्वामधिष्ठाय संभवाम्यात्ममायया ॥

prakṛtim svām adhiṣṭhāya saṃbhavāmi ātma-māyayā ||

sentences.l: Unborn although, and imperishable-in-nature, of-beings the-lord although, being — my-own nature having-taken-control-of, I-come-to-be through-my-own-power-of-illusion.
sentences.i: Although I am unborn and imperishable in nature, and the lord of all beings, I come into being by taking control of my own nature, through my own creative power.
sentences.n: Two concessive clauses frame the paradox: ajaḥ api san, 'though being unborn', and bhūtānām īśvaraḥ api san, 'though being lord of beings' (with avyaya-ātmā, 'of imperishable nature', an added epithet). Against this, saṃbhavāmi, 'I come to be', is explained not as compulsion by karma (as ordinary beings are driven, 3.5) but as a deliberate act: svāṃ prakṛtim adhiṣṭhāya, 'having mastered his own nature', through ātma-māyā, 'his own creative power' — the doctrinal basis for the avatāra teaching of the next two verses.

अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ॥

yadā yadā hi dharmasya glāniḥ bhavati bhārata |
abhyutthānam adharmasya tadā ātmānam sṛjāmi aham ||

sentences.l: Whenever indeed of dharma a fading comes to be, O Bhārata, a rising-up of adharma — then I send forth myself.
sentences.i: Whenever dharma wanes, Bhārata, and its opposite rises, I bring myself forth.
sentences.n: Yadā yadā, 'whenever, whenever' (doubled for generality), answers to tadā, 'then', in the second line — the same relative-correlative pattern seen at 3.21-22. Dharmasya glāniḥ, 'a wasting of dharma', and adharmasya abhyutthānam, 'a rising-up of adharma', stand in exact parallel. This is the poem's classic statement of periodic divine descent, completed by verse 8's statement of its threefold purpose. House rendering used per convention.

sentences.t:
परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् ।
धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे ॥

paritrāṇāya sādhūnām vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām |
dharma-saṃsthāpana-arthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge ||

sentences.l: For the rescue of the good and for the destruction of evil-doers, for the purpose of establishing dharma, I come to be age after age.
sentences.i: To rescue the good, to destroy those who do evil, and to set dharma firmly in place, I am born in every age.
sentences.n: Three parallel datives of purpose — paritrāṇāya, vināśāya, dharma-saṃsthāpana-arthāya — govern the one verb sambhavāmi. Yuge yuge, 'age after age' (another doubled word, like yadā yadā in verse 7), completes the doctrine of verse 7 with its threefold aim: protecting the good, destroying evildoers, re-establishing dharma. Together 4.7-8 are among the Gītā's most quoted verses. House rendering used per convention.

sentences.l: Birth and action, my, divine, thus who knows in-truth — having-given-up the-body, rebirth not attains; to-me he-attains, O Arjuna.
sentences.i: One who truly knows in this way my divine birth and action does not, on giving up the body, take birth again — he comes to me, Arjuna.
sentences.n: Janma and karma, both objects of vetti, are qualified as divyam, 'divine' — Kṛṣṇa's voluntary incarnation (verse 6) and its purpose (verses 7-8), not ordinary karma-driven birth and action. Knowing this tattvataḥ, 'as it truly is', is what frees one from punarjanma, 'rebirth', and grants mām eti, 'he comes to me' — the doctrine of union with Kṛṣṇa developed further in later chapters (8.5-7, 9.34, 18.65).

sentences.l: Free-from-passion-fear-and-anger, absorbed-in-me, in-me taken-refuge — many, through-the-austerity-of-knowledge purified, to-my-state-of-being have-come.
sentences.i: Many, free from passion, fear and anger, absorbed in me and taking refuge in me, purified by the discipline of knowledge, have attained my very being.
sentences.n: The promise of verse 9 is generalized to bahavaḥ, 'many' seekers across time. Vīta-rāga-bhaya-krodhāḥ, 'free from passion, fear and anger', names the threefold freedom required; jñāna-tapasā pūtāḥ, 'purified by the austerity of knowledge', names the means, recalling jñāna-yoga at 3.3. Mad-bhāvam āgatāḥ, 'have come to my very being', intensifies verse 9's mām eti.

sentences.l: Who as to-me they-approach, them so, indeed, I-favor; my path men follow, O Pārtha, in-every-way.
sentences.i: In whatever way people approach me, I reward them in that same way; men follow my path in every way, Pārtha.
sentences.n: A relative-correlative pair, ye ... yathā ... tān ... tathā (cf. yadā ... tadā, verse 7), states a striking reciprocity: bhajāmi, 'I favor, I share in return' (the root behind bhakti), meets each worshipper on the terms of their own approach. This much-debated verse is read by some as an early statement that all sincere paths, however conceived, ultimately lead to Kṛṣṇa.

sentences.t:
काङ्क्षन्तः कर्मणां सिद्धिं यजन्त इह देवताः ।
क्षिप्रं हि मानुषे लोके सिद्धिर्भवति कर्मजा ॥
sentences.tr:
kāṅkṣantaḥ karmaṇām siddhim yajante iha devatāḥ |
kṣipram hi mānuṣe loke siddhiḥ bhavati karma-jā ||

morph.gloss: to desire, long for (kāṅkṣant: present participle, nom. pl. 'desiring')
action (gen. pl. 'of actions')
success, fulfillment (acc. sg., object of kāṅkṣantaḥ)
to sacrifice, worship (yajante: present middle 3rd pl. 'they worship'; -e + i- → -a i-, cf. 3.28 vartanta)
here, in this world
deity, god (nom. pl.)
quick, swift (adverbial acc. 'quickly')
for, indeed
human, of men (loc. sg., agreeing with loke)
world (loc. sg. 'in the world')
success, attainment (nom. sg.; -iḥ + bh- → -ir bh-)
to come to be, arise (bhavati: present 3rd sg.)
action (first compound member)
born, arising from (karma-ja: 'born of action', nom. sg. fem., agreeing with siddhiḥ)

sentences.l: Desiring, of-actions the-success, they-worship here the-gods; quickly, indeed, in-the-human world, success comes-to-be, born-of-action.
sentences.i: Those who desire success in their actions worship the gods in this world, for in the human world success born of action comes quickly.
sentences.n: Yajante is the underlying form of yajanta before iha; the final -e shifts to -a before a following short vowel, the same rare sandhi already met at 3.28's vartanta. The verse candidly names a lesser motive — kāṅkṣantaḥ karmaṇāṃ siddhim, 'desiring success in action' (siddhi, 'accomplishment', distinct from phala, 'fruit', the word used for the attachment warned against in the house rendering of 2.47) — driving ordinary worship of minor deities, because such results come kṣipram, 'quickly', in the human world; Śaṅkara treats this as a description of common practice, not the poem's own recommendation.

sentences.t:
चातुर्वर्ण्यं मया सृष्टं गुणकर्मविभागशः ।
तस्य कर्तारमपि मां विद्ध्यकर्तारमव्ययम् ॥
sentences.tr:
cāturvarṇyam mayā sṛṣṭam guṇa-karma-vibhāgaśaḥ |
tasya kartāram api mām viddhi akartāram avyayam ||

morph.gloss: the fourfold class-system (abstract noun from catur-varṇa, 'the four varṇas'; acc. sg. neut.)
I (instr. sg. 'by me')
to create, emit (sṛṣṭa: past participle 'created', acc. sg. neut., agreeing with cāturvarṇyam)
one of the three guṇas (first compound member; kept untranslated per convention)
action (second compound member)
division, distinction (guṇa-karma-vibhāga: 'the division of guṇa and action', vibhāgaśaḥ: adverbial with the distributive suffix -śas, 'according to the division of')
that, it (gen. sg. 'of it', referring to cāturvarṇyam)
to do (kartṛ: agent noun 'doer', kartāram: acc. sg. 'as the doer')
although, even
I (acc. sg. 'me')
to know (viddhi: imperative 2nd sg. 'know!'; -i + a- → -y a-)
non-doer (akartāram: acc. sg. 'as the non-doer')
imperishable, unchanging (avyayam: acc. sg., agreeing with mām)

sentences.l: The-fourfold-class-system by-me [was] created, according-to-the-division-of-guṇa-and-action; of-it the-doer, although, me, know [as] the-non-doer, imperishable.
sentences.i: I created the fourfold order of classes, according to the division of the guṇas and their actions; yet know me, though its author, to be the non-doer, and imperishable.
sentences.n: Cāturvarṇyam, 'the fourfold class-system' (the four varṇas, taken up again at 18.41-44), is traced to Kṛṣṇa's own creative act, but guṇa-karma-vibhāgaśaḥ, 'according to the division of guṇa and action' — each class corresponding to a distribution of the three guṇas and its characteristic work, applying chapter 3's guṇa-doctrine (3.27-29) to society itself. The second line then applies that same doctrine to Kṛṣṇa: tasya kartāram api mām ... akartāram avyayam, 'me, though its maker, know as the non-doer, unchanging' — paralleling verse 6's claim that his own action does not bind him.

sentences.t:
न मां कर्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पृहा ।
इति मां योऽभिजानाति कर्मभिर्न स बध्यते ॥
sentences.tr:
na mām karmāṇi limpanti na me karma-phale spṛhā |
iti mām yaḥ abhijānāti karmabhiḥ na saḥ badhyate ||

morph.gloss: not
I (acc. sg. 'me')
action (nom. pl., subject of limpanti)
to stain, defile, cling to (limpanti: present 3rd pl. 'they stain')
not
I (me: enclitic gen. sg. 'my')
action (first compound member)
fruit, result (karma-phala: 'the fruit of action', loc. sg.)
longing, desire (nom. sg., 'there is longing')
thus (closing the quoted teaching)
I (acc. sg. 'me')
who (yaḥ: nom. sg. masc. relative; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
to know fully, understand (abhijānāti: present 3rd sg. 'understands')
action (instr. pl. 'by actions'; -iḥ + n- → -ir n-)
not
that, he (nom. sg. masc.)
to bind (badhyate: present passive 3rd sg. 'is bound')

sentences.l: Not me actions stain; not for-me in-the-fruit-of-action [is-there] longing. Thus who me knows-fully — by-actions not he is-bound.
sentences.i: Actions do not stain me, nor do I long for the fruit of action. Whoever knows me in this way is not bound by actions.
sentences.n: A summary statement of what verses 6 and 13 have just claimed of Kṛṣṇa: na māṃ karmāṇi limpanti, 'actions do not stain me', and na me karma-phale spṛhā, 'I have no longing for the fruit of action' — the latter echoing the house rendering of 2.47 as Kṛṣṇa's own standing example of unattached action. Iti māṃ yo 'bhijānāti, 'whoever thus knows me', extends the same release from karmic bondage (karmabhir na sa badhyate) already promised in verse 9, now grounded in this understanding of Kṛṣṇa's nature, closing the chapter's opening movement before the extended teaching on action itself resumes.

sentences.t:
एवं ज्ञात्वा कृतं कर्म पूर्वैरपि मुमुक्षुभिः ।
कुरु कर्मैव तस्मात्त्वं पूर्वैः पूर्वतरं कृतम् ॥
sentences.tr:
evam jñātvā kṛtam karma pūrvaiḥ api mumukṣubhiḥ |
kuru karma eva tasmāt tvam pūrvaiḥ pūrvataram kṛtam ||

morph.gloss: thus
to know (jñātvā: gerund 'having known [this]')
to do (kṛta: past participle 'done', nom. sg. neut., predicate with karma)
action (nom. sg., subject of kṛtam)
former, ancient (pūrvaiḥ: instr. pl., agent of the passive-sense kṛtam, 'by the ancients')
even, also (pūrvaiḥ + api → pūrvair api)
to release (mumukṣu: desiderative adjective 'desiring release', instr. pl., agreeing with pūrvaiḥ)
to do (kuru: imperative 2nd sg. 'do!')
action (acc. sg., object of kuru)
indeed (karma + eva → karmaiva)
that (tasmāt: abl. sg. 'therefore')
you (nom. sg.; -t + tv- → -t tv- written doubled)
former, ancient (instr. pl. 'by the ancients', repeated from the first line)
former (comparative pūrvatara: 'more anciently, even earlier', adverbial acc. sg. neut.)
to do (kṛta: past participle, acc. sg. neut. 'done', in apposition to karma)

sentences.l: Thus having-known, action [was] done even-by-former seekers-of-liberation; do action, indeed, you, therefore — by-the-ancients, more-anciently, done.
sentences.i: Knowing this, even the sages of old who sought liberation performed action; therefore you too should act, just as it was done by the ancients, and by those before them still.
sentences.n: Kṛtaṃ karma pūrvaiḥ, 'action was done by the ancients' (the past participle kṛtam functioning almost as a finite verb, with the agent pūrvaiḥ in the instrumental, as with any passive participle), continues the argument of verses 9-14 into direct address: even mumukṣubhiḥ, 'those desiring liberation' (from muc, the poem's first use of this term), still acted. Pūrvaiḥ pūrvataraṃ kṛtam, 'done by the ancients, done still more anciently', doubles the appeal to precedent, much as ch. 3's Janaka argument (3.20) did.

sentences.t:
किं कर्म किमकर्मेति कवयोऽप्यत्र मोहिताः ।
तत्ते कर्म प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात् ॥
sentences.tr:
kim karma kim akarma iti kavayaḥ api atra mohitāḥ |
tat te karma pravakṣyāmi yat jñātvā mokṣyase aśubhāt ||

morph.gloss: what?
action (nom. sg., predicate: 'what is action?')
what? (repeated)
inaction (akarma: nom. sg. neut., predicate 'what is inaction?')
thus (closes the quoted question; akarma + iti → akarmeti)
poet, sage, seer (kavayaḥ: nom. pl.; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
even (kavayo 'pi + atra → kavayo 'py atra, -i + a- → -y a-)
here, in this matter
to be confused (mohita: causative past participle 'confused, deluded', nom. pl.)
that (tat: acc. sg. neut., object of pravakṣyāmi)
you (te: enclitic dat. sg. 'to you')
action (acc. sg., in apposition to tat)
to declare, teach (pravakṣyāmi: future 1st sg. 'I will declare')
which (yat: acc. sg. neut. relative, object of jñātvā)
to know (jñātvā: gerund 'having known'; -t + j- → -j j- written doubled)
to release (mokṣyase: future middle 2nd sg. 'you shall be freed'; -e + a- → -e with avagraha)
evil, misfortune (aśubhāt: abl. sg. 'from evil')

sentences.l: What [is] action? What [is] inaction? — thus even-the-wise, here, [are] confused. That to-you action I-will-declare, knowing which you-will-be-freed from-evil.
sentences.i: 'What is action? What is inaction?' Even the wise are confused about this. I will explain to you what action is, and knowing it you will be freed from evil.
sentences.n: Kavayaḥ, 'seers, sages' (kavi, MW's older sense of an inspired poet-seer, not merely 'poet'), admits that even they are mohitāḥ, 'confused', about the very distinction the chapter is about to draw — kiṃ karma kim akarma, 'what is action, what is inaction', posed as two nominal questions closed by iti. Aśubhāt, 'from evil, misfortune', names the reward of understanding it: mokṣyase, 'you will be released', from the same root as mumukṣu in verse 15.

sentences.t:
कर्मणो ह्यपि बोद्धव्यं बोद्धव्यं च विकर्मणः ।
अकर्मणश्च बोद्धव्यं गहना कर्मणो गतिः ॥
sentences.tr:
karmaṇaḥ hi api boddhavyam boddhavyam ca vikarmaṇaḥ |
akarmaṇaḥ ca boddhavyam gahanā karmaṇaḥ gatiḥ ||

morph.gloss: action (gen. sg. 'of action, what action is'; -aḥ + h- → -o h-)
for, indeed (hi + a- → hy a-)
even
to know, understand (boddhavya: gerundive 'is to be known, must be understood', nom. sg. neut., impersonal)
to know, understand (boddhavya: gerundive, nom. sg. neut., repeated)
and
wrong action, forbidden action (gen. sg. 'of wrong action')
inaction (akarmaṇaḥ: gen. sg. 'of inaction'; -aḥ + c- → -aś c-)
and
to know, understand (boddhavya: gerundive, nom. sg. neut.)
deep, dense, impenetrable (nom. sg. fem., agreeing with gatiḥ)
action (gen. sg.; -aḥ + g- → -o g-)
to go (gati: 'course, movement, way', nom. sg. fem.)

sentences.l: Of-action, indeed, even, [something] is-to-be-known, and is-to-be-known of-wrong-action; and of-inaction is-to-be-known — deep [is] the-course of-action.
sentences.i: One must understand what action is, and what wrong action is, and what inaction is as well — for the way of action is hard to fathom.
sentences.n: The verse names a third term beside karma and akarma: vikarma, 'wrong, forbidden action' — introduced here for the first time in the poem. Boddhavyam, 'is to be known', a gerundive used impersonally three times, states that all three must be understood before the paradox of the next verse can make sense; gahanā karmaṇo gatiḥ, 'the course of action is deep [i.e. hard to fathom]', is Kṛṣṇa's own warning that what follows is subtle.

sentences.t:
कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः ।
स बुद्धिमान्मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत् ॥
sentences.tr:
karmaṇi akarma yaḥ paśyet akarmaṇi ca karma yaḥ |
saḥ buddhimān manuṣyeṣu saḥ yuktaḥ kṛtsna-karma-kṛt ||

morph.gloss: action (karmaṇi: loc. sg. 'in action')
inaction (akarma: acc. sg. neut., object of paśyet; karmaṇi + a- → karmaṇy a-)
who (nom. sg. masc. relative)
to see (paśyet: optative 3rd sg. 'should see'; -t + a- → -d a-)
inaction (akarmaṇi: loc. sg. 'in inaction')
and
action (acc. sg., object of paśyet, understood repeated)
who (nom. sg. masc. relative, repeated)
that, he (nom. sg. masc.; visarga dropped before b-)
possessed of understanding, wise (buddhimān: nom. sg. masc.)
man (manuṣyeṣu: loc. pl. 'among men')
that, he (nom. sg. masc.; visarga dropped before y-)
to join, discipline (yukta: past participle 'disciplined, one who has attained yoga', nom. sg.)
whole, entire (first compound member)
action (second compound member)
doer, one who does (kṛtsna-karma-kṛt: 'one who has accomplished all action', nom. sg.)

sentences.l: Who inaction-in-action sees, and who action-in-inaction — he [is] wise among-men, he [is] disciplined, a-doer-of-all-action.
sentences.i: The one who sees inaction in action, and action in inaction, is wise among men; he is disciplined, and he has accomplished everything there is to do.
sentences.n: The chapter's most quoted paradox, built on the three terms just distinguished in verse 17: karmaṇy akarma ... akarmaṇi ca karma, 'inaction in action ... action in inaction', a chiastic double relative clause (yaḥ ... yaḥ) resolved only by identifying true action and inaction with attachment and its absence, not with outward movement or stillness — the same point ch. 3.4-7 made about the hypocrite who is outwardly still but inwardly active. Kṛtsna-karma-kṛt, 'one who has done all action', restates ch. 3.19's kāryaṃ karma in a single compound.

sentences.t:
यस्य सर्वे समारम्भाः कामसंकल्पवर्जिताः ।
ज्ञानाग्निदग्धकर्माणं तमाहुः पण्डितं बुधाः ॥
sentences.tr:
yasya sarve samārambhāḥ kāma-saṃkalpa-varjitāḥ |
jñāna-agni-dagdha-karmāṇam tam āhuḥ paṇḍitam budhāḥ ||

morph.gloss: who (gen. sg. 'whose')
all (nom. pl., agreeing with samārambhāḥ)
to undertake (samārambha: 'undertaking', nom. pl.)
desire (first compound member)
intention, purpose, resolve (second compound member)
devoid of, free from (kāma-saṃkalpa-varjita: 'free from desire and intention', nom. pl.)
knowledge (first compound member)
fire (jñāna-agni: 'the fire of knowledge', second member; jñāna + a- → jñānā-)
burnt (past participle of dah, third member)
action (jñānāgni-dagdha-karman: 'whose actions are burnt up by the fire of knowledge', acc. sg., agreeing with tam)
that, him (tam: acc. sg.)
to say, call (āhuḥ: perfect 3rd pl. used as present 'they call')
learned, a scholar, a wise man (acc. sg., predicate of āhuḥ, 'they call him "wise"')
to know (budha: 'the wise, those who know', nom. pl., subject of āhuḥ)

sentences.l: Whose all undertakings [are] free-from-desire-and-intention — him, whose-action-is-burnt-by-the-fire-of-knowledge, they-call learned, the-wise.
sentences.i: The wise call him learned whose every undertaking is free of desire and intention, and whose actions have been consumed by the fire of knowledge.
sentences.n: Jñānāgni-dagdha-karmāṇam, 'whose action is burnt by the fire of knowledge', is the chapter's first use of the jñānāgni image, an image the poem returns to later in this chapter (v. 37, in the next batch); saṃkalpa, 'intention, deliberate resolve' (distinct from mere kāma, 'desire'), pairs with it to describe what such action lacks. Paṇḍitam, 'learned, wise', echoes 2.11's first use of the term for one who truly understands, rather than merely knows facts.

sentences.t:
त्यक्त्वा कर्मफलासङ्गं नित्यतृप्तो निराश्रयः ।
कर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्तोऽपि नैव किंचित्करोति सः ॥
sentences.tr:
tyaktvā karma-phala-āsaṅgam nitya-tṛptaḥ nirāśrayaḥ |
karmaṇi abhipravṛttaḥ api na eva kiṃcit karoti saḥ ||

morph.gloss: to abandon (tyaktvā: gerund 'having abandoned')
action (first compound member)
fruit (second compound member)
attachment, clinging (karma-phala-āsaṅga: 'attachment to the fruit of action', acc. sg., object of tyaktvā; phala + ā- → phalā-)
eternal, constant (first compound member)
satisfied, content (nitya-tṛpta: 'ever content', nom. sg.; -aḥ before n- → -o)
without support, without refuge (nom. sg.)
action (karmaṇi: loc. sg.; -i + a- → -y a-)
to be engaged, set about (abhipravṛtta: past participle 'engaged, set about', nom. sg.; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
even, although
not (na + e- → nai-)
at all, indeed
anything (acc. sg. neut.)
to do (karoti: present 3rd sg. 'does')
that, he (nom. sg. masc.)

sentences.l: Having-abandoned attachment-to-the-fruit-of-action, ever-content, without-support — though engaged in-action, not-at-all anything does he.
sentences.i: Having given up attachment to the fruit of his actions, ever content and dependent on nothing, he does nothing at all, even while he is engaged in action.
sentences.n: Karma-phala-āsaṅgam, 'attachment to the fruit of action', restates the house rendering of 2.47 in compound form. Karmaṇy abhipravṛttaḥ api naiva kiṃcit karoti, '[though] engaged in action, he does nothing at all', is a deliberate paradox like verse 18's: 'does nothing' means he incurs no fresh result, not that he is physically idle, as the next two verses go on to make concrete.

sentences.t:
निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा त्यक्तसर्वपरिग्रहः ।
शारीरं केवलं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
sentences.tr:
nirāśīḥ yata-citta-ātmā tyakta-sarva-parigrahaḥ |
śārīram kevalam karma kurvan na āpnoti kilbiṣam ||

morph.gloss: without desire, without hope of gain (nirāśīḥ: nom. sg.; -īḥ + y- → -īr y-)
restrained, controlled (past participle of yam, first compound member)
mind, thought (second compound member)
self (yata-citta-ātman: 'whose mind and self are controlled', nom. sg.; citta + ā- → cittā-)
abandoned, given up (first compound member)
all (second compound member)
possession, acquisition, grasping (tyakta-sarva-parigraha: 'having given up all possessions', nom. sg.)
bodily, pertaining to the body (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with karma)
mere, only (acc. sg. neut.)
action (acc. sg., object of kurvan)
to do (kurvan: present participle, nom. sg. 'doing'; kurvan + na → kurvanna, -n + n- written doubled)
not
to attain, incur (āpnoti: present 3rd sg. 'incurs'; na + ā- → nā-)
sin, fault (acc. sg., object of āpnoti)

sentences.l: Without-hope, restrained-in-mind-and-self, having-abandoned-all-possessions — mere bodily action doing, he-incurs-not sin.
sentences.i: Free of expectation, his mind and self restrained, having given up all possessions, doing only what the body requires, he incurs no fault.
sentences.n: Śārīraṃ kevalaṃ karma, 'mere bodily action', names the minimal residue of activity even such a man still performs — bare bodily necessity, the same idea as ch. 3.8's śarīra-yātrā, 'the maintenance of the body' — without incurring kilbiṣam, 'sin, moral fault' (cf. 3.13). Nir-āśis, 'without hope [of gain]', and tyakta-sarva-parigrahaḥ, 'having renounced all possessions', sharpen verse 20's nirāśrayaḥ into concrete terms.

sentences.t:
यदृच्छालाभसंतुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः ।
समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते ॥
sentences.tr:
yadṛcchā-lābha-saṃtuṣṭaḥ dvandva-atītaḥ vimatsaraḥ |
samaḥ siddhau asiddhau ca kṛtvā api na nibadhyate ||

morph.gloss: chance, spontaneous occurrence (first compound member)
gain, acquisition (second compound member)
satisfied, content (yadṛcchā-lābha-saṃtuṣṭa: 'content with what comes by chance', nom. sg.; -aḥ before d- → -o)
a pair (of opposites, such as pleasure and pain)
gone beyond, transcended (past participle of ati-i; dvandva-atīta: 'beyond the pairs of opposites', nom. sg.; dvandva + a- → dvandvā-; -aḥ before v- → -o)
free from envy, without malice (nom. sg.)
equal, the same (nom. sg.)
success, accomplishment (siddhau: loc. sg. 'in success')
failure, non-accomplishment (asiddhau: loc. sg. 'in failure'; -au + a- → -āv a-)
and
to do (kṛtvā: gerund 'having done, having acted')
even (kṛtvā + api → kṛtvāpi)
not
to bind (nibadhyate: present passive 3rd sg. 'is bound')

sentences.l: Content-with-gain-that-comes-unsought, beyond-the-pairs-of-opposites, free-from-envy; equal in-success and-in-failure — even having-acted, he-is-not bound.
sentences.i: Content with whatever comes unsought, beyond the pairs of opposites, free of envy, equal in success and failure — even when he acts, he is not bound.
sentences.n: Dvandva, 'a pair' (here of opposites such as pleasure and pain, heat and cold), is a technical term the poem develops further in later chapters (7.27-28, 15.5); samaḥ siddhāv asiddhau ca, 'equal in success and failure', restates in explicit terms the evenness of mind the house rendering of 2.47 already implied. Kṛtvā api na nibadhyate, 'even having acted, he is not bound', is the plainest statement yet of the chapter's central claim.

sentences.t:
गतसङ्गस्य मुक्तस्य ज्ञानावस्थितचेतसः ।
यज्ञायाचरतः कर्म समग्रं प्रविलीयते ॥
sentences.tr:
gata-saṅgasya muktasya jñāna-avasthita-cetasaḥ |
yajñāya ācarataḥ karma samagram pravilīyate ||

morph.gloss: gone (past participle of gam, first compound member)
attachment, clinging (gata-saṅga: 'one whose attachment is gone', gen. sg.)
to release (mukta: past participle 'liberated, freed', gen. sg.)
knowledge (first compound member; jñāna + a- → jñānā-)
to be established, fixed (avasthita: past participle, second compound member)
mind (jñāna-avasthita-cetas: 'whose mind is established in knowledge', gen. sg.)
sacrifice (yajñāya: dat. sg. 'for the sake of sacrifice')
to act, perform (ācarataḥ: present participle, gen. sg. 'of one who acts, performing'; yajñāya + ā- → yajñāyā-)
action (nom. sg., subject of pravilīyate)
whole, entire (nom. sg. neut., agreeing with karma)
to melt away, dissolve completely (pravilīyate: present passive 3rd sg. 'is dissolved, melts away entirely')

sentences.l: Of-one-whose-attachment-is-gone, of-the-liberated, whose-mind-is-established-in-knowledge — acting for-the-sake-of-sacrifice, action, wholly, dissolves-away.
sentences.i: For one who is free of attachment, liberated, his mind fixed in knowledge, and who acts only for the sake of sacrifice — his action dissolves away completely.
sentences.n: Four descriptions of the same man (gata-saṅgasya, muktasya, jñāna-avasthita-cetasaḥ, ācarataḥ, all genitive) build up to a single claim about karma, the grammatical subject: samagraṃ pravilīyate, 'dissolves away entirely' — a stronger image than verses 20-22's 'not bound', reserved for one who, like ch. 3.9's yajñārthāt karma, acts specifically yajñāya, 'for sacrifice'. This closes the run of descriptions of the liberated actor (vv. 19-23) and turns the chapter, from verse 24, to sacrifice itself.

sentences.t:
ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्म हविर्ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम् ।
ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना ॥
sentences.tr:
brahma arpaṇam brahma haviḥ brahma-agnau brahmaṇā hutam |
brahma eva tena gantavyam brahma-karma-samādhinā ||

morph.gloss: brahman (kept untranslated; nom. sg. neut.)
the act or instrument of offering (arpaṇam: nom. sg. neut., predicate: 'the offering is brahman')
brahman (nom. sg. neut., predicate continues: 'brahman is the oblation')
oblation, the substance offered (haviḥ: nom. sg. neut.; -iḥ + b- → -ir b-)
brahman (first compound member, kept untranslated)
fire (brahma-agni: 'the fire that is brahman', loc. sg. 'into the brahman-fire'; brahma + a- → brahmā-)
brahman (instr. sg. 'by brahman', the agent who offers)
to offer, pour as oblation (huta: past participle 'offered, poured', nom. sg. neut., completing the series 'offered by brahman')
brahman (nom. sg. neut., now named as the goal)
alone, itself (brahma + eva → brahmaiva)
that, he (tena: instr. sg. 'by him', the agent of the gerundive gantavyam)
to go (gantavya: gerundive 'is to be reached, attained', nom. sg. neut., agreeing with brahma)
brahman (first compound member)
action (second compound member; brahma-karman: 'action [known as] brahman')
absorption, deep concentration (brahma-karma-samādhi: 'absorption in brahman-action', instr. sg., describing tena)

sentences.l: Brahman [is] the-offering, brahman [is] the-oblation, into-the-brahman-fire, by-brahman, offered; brahman alone, by-him, [is] to-be-reached, whose-absorption-is-in-brahman-action.
sentences.i: The offering is brahman, the oblation is brahman, poured by brahman into the fire that is brahman; and brahman alone is what is reached by one whose action is wholly absorbed in brahman.
sentences.n: One of the poem's most famous sentences, built entirely on the word brahman (kept untranslated), repeated six times, each in a different grammatical role: nominative as the offering-vessel (arpaṇam) and again as the oblation (havis), locative as the fire it is poured into (brahmāgnau), instrumental as the one who pours it (brahmaṇā), nominative once more (with eva) as the goal reached, and finally instrumental in the closing compound brahma-karma-samādhinā, 'absorbed in brahman-action', describing the person who reaches it. The pattern states that every element of the sacrificial act — instrument, material, fire, agent and result — is nothing other than brahman; recognizing this, as verse 23 already said, dissolves the action away, and the one so absorbed reaches brahman itself. The teaching echoes ch. 3.15's brahmodbhavaṃ karma, which likewise traced karma back to brahman.

sentences.t:
दैवमेवापरे यज्ञं योगिनः पर्युपासते ।
ब्रह्माग्नावपरे यज्ञं यज्ञेनैवोपजुह्वति ॥
sentences.tr:
daivam eva apare yajñam yoginaḥ paryupāsate |
brahma-agnau apare yajñam yajñena eva upajuhvati ||

morph.gloss: divine, pertaining to the gods (daivam: acc. sg. neut., agreeing with yajñam, 'sacrifice directed to the gods')
alone, only
other (apare: nom. pl. 'others, some'; eva + a- → evā-)
sacrifice (acc. sg., object of paryupāsate)
one who practices yoga, a yogin (nom. pl.)
to wait upon, worship, attend to (paryupāsate: present middle 3rd pl. 'attend upon, worship')
brahman (first compound member, kept untranslated)
fire (brahma-agni: 'the fire that is brahman', loc. sg. 'into the brahman-fire')
other (apare: nom. pl. 'others'; agnau + a- → agnāv a-)
sacrifice (acc. sg., object of upajuhvati)
sacrifice (yajñena: instr. sg. 'with sacrifice itself')
alone, itself (yajñena + eva → yajñenaiva)
to offer up, pour as oblation (upajuhvati: present 3rd pl. 'they offer up'; eva + u- → evo-)

sentences.l: The-divine sacrifice alone, some, yogins, attend-upon; others, into-the-brahman-fire, the-sacrifice, by-sacrifice-itself, offer-up.
sentences.i: Some yogins worship only through sacrifice offered to the gods; others offer sacrifice itself as an oblation into the fire that is brahman.
sentences.n: This opens the chapter's catalogue of the many things called yajña, 'sacrifice' (through verse 33, continuing into the next batch), starting with the plainest form — daivam yajñam, ritual offering to the gods — set against those who instead treat the very act of sacrifice as an oblation poured into the brahman-fire just described in verse 24. Juhvati and its compound upajuhvati, 'they offer, pour as oblation', are the verbs that will recur through verse 27.

sentences.t:
श्रोत्रादीनीन्द्रियाण्यन्ये संयमाग्निषु जुह्वति ।
शब्दादीन्विषयानन्य इन्द्रियाग्निषु जुह्वति ॥
sentences.tr:
śrotra-ādīni indriyāṇi anye saṃyama-agniṣu juhvati |
śabda-ādīn viṣayān anye indriya-agniṣu juhvati ||

morph.gloss: the organ of hearing, the ear (first compound member)
beginning (śrotra-ādi: 'beginning with hearing, i.e. and the rest', acc. pl. neut., agreeing with indriyāṇi; ādīni + i- → ādīny i-)
sense-organ (indriyāṇi: acc. pl., object of juhvati)
other (anye: nom. pl. 'others'; indriyāṇi + a- → indriyāṇy a-)
to restrain (saṃyama: 'restraint, control', first compound member)
fire (saṃyama-agni: 'the fires of restraint', loc. pl.; saṃyama + a- → saṃyamā-)
to offer, pour as oblation (juhvati: present 3rd pl. 'they offer')
sound (first compound member)
beginning (śabda-ādi: 'beginning with sound', acc. pl., agreeing with viṣayān)
a sense-object (viṣayān: acc. pl., object of juhvati)
other (anye: nom. pl. 'others'; -e + i- → -a i-)
sense-organ (first compound member)
fire (indriya-agni: 'the fires of the senses', loc. pl.; indriya + a- → indriyā-)
to offer (juhvati: present 3rd pl. 'they offer')

sentences.l: The-senses-beginning-with-hearing, others, into-the-fires-of-restraint, offer; the-objects-beginning-with-sound, others, into-the-fires-of-the-senses, offer.
sentences.i: Some offer the senses themselves, beginning with hearing, as oblations into the fires of restraint; others offer the objects of sense, beginning with sound, into the fires of the senses.
sentences.n: Śrotra-ādīni and śabda-ādīn both use ādi, 'beginning [with]', the standard way of naming an open list by its first member (as with avyaktādīni bhūtāni at 2.28). The verse contrasts two disciplines: one offers the senses themselves into 'the fires of restraint' (withdrawal from sense-activity), the other offers the sense-objects into 'the fires of the senses' themselves (controlled engagement rather than withdrawal) — the same two postures already weighed against each other in ch. 3.6-7.

sentences.t:
सर्वाणीन्द्रियकर्माणि प्राणकर्माणि चापरे ।
आत्मसंयमयोगाग्नौ जुह्वति ज्ञानदीपिते ॥
sentences.tr:
sarvāṇi indriya-karmāṇi prāṇa-karmāṇi ca apare |
ātma-saṃyama-yoga-agnau juhvati jñāna-dīpite ||

morph.gloss: all (sarvāṇi: acc. pl. neut., agreeing with karmāṇi; -i + i- → -ī-)
sense-organ (first compound member)
action (indriya-karman: 'the actions of the senses', acc. pl.)
the outward, upward breath (first compound member)
action (prāṇa-karman: 'the actions, the functioning, of the vital breaths', acc. pl.)
and (ca + a- → cā-)
other (apare: nom. pl. 'others')
self (first compound member)
restraint (second compound member)
yoga, discipline (ātma-saṃyama-yoga: 'the discipline of self-restraint', third member)
fire (ātma-saṃyama-yoga-agni: 'the fire of the discipline of self-restraint', loc. sg.; yoga + a- → yogā-)
to offer (juhvati: present 3rd pl. 'they offer')
knowledge (first compound member)
kindled, lit (causative past participle of dīp; jñāna-dīpita: 'kindled by knowledge', loc. sg., agreeing with agnau)

sentences.l: All the-actions-of-the-senses, and the-actions-of-the-life-breaths, others, into-the-fire-of-the-discipline-of-self-restraint, kindled-by-knowledge, offer.
sentences.i: Others offer all the workings of the senses and of the vital breaths into the fire of the discipline of self-restraint, kindled by knowledge.
sentences.n: Prāṇa-karmāṇi, 'the actions of the vital breaths', extends verse 26's offering of the senses to prāṇa itself, the breath regulated by the practice taken up directly in the verses just after this batch (29-30). The fire receiving both offerings is now named outright as ātma-saṃyama-yoga, 'the discipline of self-restraint', and called jñāna-dīpite, 'kindled by knowledge' — tying this whole catalogue back to the jñānāgni, 'fire of knowledge', of verse 19.

sentences.t:
द्रव्ययज्ञास्तपोयज्ञा योगयज्ञास्तथापरे ।
स्वाध्यायज्ञानयज्ञाश्च यतयः संशितव्रताः ॥
sentences.tr:
dravya-yajñāḥ tapo-yajñāḥ yoga-yajñāḥ tathā apare |
svādhyāya-jñāna-yajñāḥ ca yatayaḥ saṃśita-vratāḥ ||

morph.gloss: substance, material wealth (first compound member)
sacrifice (dravya-yajña: 'sacrifice performed with material offerings', nom. pl.; -āḥ + t- → -ās t-)
austerity, ascetic heat (first compound member; tapaḥ + y- → tapo y-)
sacrifice (tapo-yajña: 'sacrifice performed by austerity', nom. pl.; -āḥ before y- → -ā)
yoga, discipline (first compound member)
sacrifice (yoga-yajña: 'sacrifice performed by yoga', nom. pl.; -āḥ + t- → -ās t-)
likewise (tathā + a- → tathā-)
other (apare: nom. pl. 'others')
one's own recitation, private study of the Veda (svādhyāya: first compound member; sva + a- → svā-)
knowledge (second compound member)
sacrifice (svādhyāya-jñāna-yajña: 'sacrifice performed by study and by knowledge', nom. pl.; -āḥ + c- → -āś c-)
and
an ascetic, one who has restrained himself (nom. pl.)
sharpened, made rigorous (past participle of sam-śo, first compound member)
vow (saṃśita-vrata: 'of rigorous vows', nom. pl.)

sentences.l: Sacrificers-by-substance, sacrificers-by-austerity, sacrificers-by-yoga, likewise, others; sacrificers-by-study-and-knowledge, and — ascetics, of-rigorous-vows.
sentences.i: Some sacrifice with material offerings, some through austerity, some through the discipline of yoga, and others still through study and the pursuit of knowledge — all of them ascetics bound by rigorous vows.
sentences.n: A list of yajña compounds, each a distinct karmadhāraya naming sacrifice by its means — dravya (material substance), tapas (austerity), yoga, and svādhyāya-jñāna (recitation and knowledge) — continuing the catalogue begun at verse 25 and carried on with the breath-offerings of verses 29-30 (the next batch). Yatayaḥ saṃśita-vratāḥ, 'ascetics of sharpened vows', names all these practitioners together as of one kind, however different their chosen means.

sentences.t:
अपाने जुह्वति प्राणं प्राणेऽपानं तथापरे ।
प्राणापानगती रुद्ध्वा प्राणायामपरायणाः ॥
sentences.tr:
apāne juhvati prāṇam prāṇe apānam tathā apare |
prāṇa-apāna-gatī ruddhvā prāṇa-āyāma-parāyaṇāḥ ||

morph.gloss: the downward breath (loc. sg. 'into apāna')
to offer as oblation, sacrifice (juhvati: present 3rd pl. 'they offer')
the outward, upward breath (acc. sg., object of juhvati)
the outward, upward breath (prāṇe: loc. sg. 'into prāṇa'; prāṇe + a- → prāṇe' with avagraha)
the downward breath (apānam: acc. sg.)
likewise, so (tathā + apare fuse to tathāpare, ā + a → ā)
other (apare: nom. pl. 'others')
the outward, upward breath (first compound member)
the downward breath (second compound member; prāṇa + apāna → prāṇāpāna at the hyphen)
course, motion (gatī: acc. dual 'the two courses', object of ruddhvā)
to obstruct, block, restrain (ruddhvā: gerund 'having restrained')
the outward, upward breath (first compound member)
restraint, extension (prāṇa-āyāma: 'breath-restraint', second compound member; prāṇa + āyāma → prāṇāyāma at the hyphen)
intent upon, wholly devoted to (parāyaṇāḥ: nom. pl., agreeing with apare)

sentences.l: Into-apāna they-offer prāṇa, into-prāṇa apāna — likewise others; the-two-courses-of-prāṇa-and-apāna having-restrained, intent-on-breath-restraint.
sentences.i: Some offer the outward breath into the downward breath, and others, in the same way, offer the downward breath into the outward; others still block the passage of both breaths and give themselves wholly to breath-restraint.
sentences.n: Continuing the catalog of sacrifices opened at verse 24 (each kind of austerity and study already named there and at verse 28 counted as a yajña), this verse turns specifically to breath-control as an inner sacrifice: prāṇa and apāna are two of the five vital breaths (prāṇa the outward/upward breath, apāna the downward), and offering one into the other names two complementary breathing exercises, exhalation and inhalation each treated as an oblation. Prāṇāyāma-parāyaṇāḥ, 'devoted to breath-restraint', names a further group who instead block both breaths' movement outright.

sentences.t:
अपरे नियताहाराः प्राणान्प्राणेषु जुह्वति ।
सर्वेऽप्येते यज्ञविदो यज्ञक्षपितकल्मषाः ॥
sentences.tr:
apare niyata-āhārāḥ prāṇān prāṇeṣu juhvati |
sarve api ete yajña-vidaḥ yajña-kṣapita-kalmaṣāḥ ||

morph.gloss: other (nom. pl. 'others', subject)
to restrain, regulate, prescribe (niyata: past participle 'regulated, restricted', first compound member)
food, diet (niyata-āhāra: 'of regulated diet', nom. pl. bahuvrīhi; niyata + āhāra → niyatāhāra at the hyphen)
the outward, upward breath (prāṇān: acc. pl., object of juhvati)
the outward, upward breath (prāṇeṣu: loc. pl. 'into the breaths')
to offer as oblation (juhvati: present 3rd pl. 'they offer')
all (sarve: nom. pl.; sarve + a- → sarve' with avagraha)
even, also (api + e- → ye-, semivowel before ete)
this (ete: nom. pl. 'these')
sacrifice (first compound member)
knowing (vidaḥ: 'knowers', yajña-vid: 'knowers of sacrifice', nom. pl.; -aḥ + y- → -o y-)
sacrifice (first compound member)
to destroy, wear away (kṣapita: causative past participle 'worn away, destroyed', second compound member)
sin, taint (yajña-kṣapita-kalmaṣa: 'whose sins are destroyed by sacrifice', nom. pl. bahuvrīhi)

sentences.l: Others, of-regulated-diet, the-breaths into-the-breaths offer; all these, indeed, [are] knowers-of-sacrifice, whose-sins-are-destroyed-by-sacrifice.
sentences.i: Others, restricting their food, offer their very breaths into their breaths; all of these are knowers of sacrifice, their sins consumed by it.
sentences.n: This closes the catalog of many forms of sacrifice begun at verse 24: niyatāhārāḥ, 'of restricted diet', names a further ascetic discipline alongside verse 29's breath-exercises, and prāṇān prāṇeṣu juhvati, 'offer the breaths into the breaths', restates that same practice without singling out prāṇa and apāna. Yajña-vidaḥ, 'knowers of sacrifice', and yajña-kṣapita-kalmaṣāḥ, 'whose sins are worn away by sacrifice' (echoing 3.13's yajña-śiṣṭāśinaḥ ... mucyante sarva-kilbiṣaiḥ), sum up the whole list: whatever its form, sacrifice performed with understanding purifies.

sentences.t:
यज्ञशिष्टामृतभुजो यान्ति ब्रह्म सनातनम् ।
नायं लोकोऽस्त्ययज्ञस्य कुतोऽन्यः कुरुसत्तम ॥
sentences.tr:
yajña-śiṣṭa-amṛta-bhujaḥ yānti brahma sanātanam |
na ayam lokaḥ asti ayajñasya kutaḥ anyaḥ kuru-sattama ||

morph.gloss: sacrifice (first compound member)
remainder, what is left over (second compound member)
nectar, ambrosia; the deathless (third compound member; śiṣṭa + amṛta → śiṣṭāmṛta at the hyphen)
eater, enjoyer (yajña-śiṣṭa-amṛta-bhuj: 'eaters of the nectar-remnant of sacrifice', nom. pl., subject of yānti; -aḥ + y- → -o y-)
to go (yānti: present 3rd pl. 'they go')
brahman (acc. sg. neut., object of yānti; kept untranslated per convention)
eternal, everlasting (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with brahma)
not (na + a- → nā-)
this (ayam: nom. sg. masc.)
world (lokaḥ: nom. sg.; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
to be, exist (asti: present 3rd sg. 'there is'; asti + a- → asty a-)
one without sacrifice, a non-sacrificer (ayajñasya: gen. sg. 'for the non-sacrificer')
whence? from where? (kutaḥ: -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
other (anyaḥ: nom. sg.)
the Kuru clan (first compound member)
best, most excellent (superlative of sant; kuru-sattama: 'best of the Kurus', vocative, addressed to Arjuna)

sentences.l: Eaters-of-the-nectar-remnant-of-sacrifice go to-brahman, eternal; not this world there-is for-the-non-sacrificer — whence another, O best-of-the-Kurus?
sentences.i: Those who eat the nectar left over from sacrifice reach the eternal brahman; but for one who offers no sacrifice at all, even this world is not truly his, let alone the world beyond — best of the Kurus.
sentences.n: This concludes the whole sacrifice-teaching begun at verse 9 with its reward, and by contrast its absence: yajña-śiṣṭa-amṛta-bhujaḥ, 'eaters of the nectar-remnant of sacrifice' (echoing 3.13's yajña-śiṣṭāśinaḥ, now with amṛta, 'nectar, the deathless', added), reach brahma sanātanam, 'eternal brahman'. Ayajñasya, 'for one without sacrifice', is denied even nāyaṃ lokaḥ, 'this very world', so kuto 'nyaḥ, 'how much less another' — an argument from the lesser case to the greater. Kuru-sattama, 'best of the Kurus', is a new epithet of Arjuna in this chapter.

sentences.t:
एवं बहुविधा यज्ञा वितता ब्रह्मणो मुखे ।
कर्मजान्विद्धि तान्सर्वानेवं ज्ञात्वा विमोक्ष्यसे ॥
sentences.tr:
evam bahu-vidhāḥ yajñāḥ vitatāḥ brahmaṇaḥ mukhe |
karma-jān viddhi tān sarvān evam jñātvā vimokṣyase ||

morph.gloss: thus
many (first compound member)
kind, sort (bahu-vidhā: 'of many kinds', nom. pl., agreeing with yajñāḥ; -āḥ before y- dropped)
sacrifice (nom. pl.; -āḥ before v- dropped)
to spread out, extend (vitata: past participle 'spread out, laid out', nom. pl.; -āḥ before b- dropped)
brahman (gen. sg. 'of brahman'; kept untranslated per convention; -aḥ + m- → -o m-)
mouth, face (loc. sg. 'in the mouth')
action (first compound member)
born (karma-ja: 'born of action', jān: acc. pl., object of viddhi)
to know (viddhi: imperative 2nd sg. 'know!')
that, these (tān: acc. pl., referring to the sacrifices)
all (sarvān: acc. pl.)
thus
to know (jñātvā: gerund 'having known')
to release, free (vimokṣyase: future middle 2nd sg. 'you shall be released')

sentences.l: Thus many-kinds-of sacrifices [are] spread-out in-the-mouth of-brahman; born-of-action know them all — thus having-known, you-shall-be-released.
sentences.i: Thus many kinds of sacrifice are laid out in the mouth of brahman; know that all of them are born of action, and knowing this, you shall be set free.
sentences.n: A summary of the whole catalog just given (verses 24-30): brahmaṇo mukhe, 'in the mouth of brahman', most likely continues the sense of brahman as the Veda already used at 3.15 (Śaṅkara reads it as 'proclaimed by the Veda'), rather than the cosmic absolute. Karma-jān, 'born of action', reduces every form just listed to a single source, closing the ring back to 3.15's own chain (karma to brahman to the imperishable) and preparing the sharper ranking of action against knowledge that follows.

sentences.t:
श्रेयान्द्रव्यमयाद्यज्ञाज्ज्ञानयज्ञः परन्तप ।
सर्वं कर्माखिलं पार्थ ज्ञाने परिसमाप्यते ॥
sentences.tr:
śreyān dravya-mayāt yajñāt jñāna-yajñaḥ parantapa |
sarvam karma akhilam pārtha jñāne parisamāpyate ||

morph.gloss: better, more excellent (comparative; śreyān: nom. sg. masc., predicate)
substance, material (first compound member)
consisting of, made of (dravya-maya: 'consisting of material substance', dravyamayāt: abl. sg.; dravyamayāt + y- → dravyamayād y-)
sacrifice (yajñāt: abl. sg. 'than [material] sacrifice'; yajñāt + j- → yajñāj j-)
knowledge (first compound member)
sacrifice (jñāna-yajña: 'the sacrifice of knowledge', nom. sg., subject)
'scorcher of the foe', an epithet of Arjuna (vocative)
all (nom. sg. neut., agreeing with karma)
action (karma: nom. sg. neut.; karma + a- → karmā-)
entire, whole (akhilam: nom. sg. neut., in apposition to karma)
'son of Pṛthā', Arjuna (vocative)
knowledge (loc. sg.)
to be completely concluded, culminate (parisamāpyate: present passive 3rd sg.)

sentences.l: Better than-the-sacrifice-consisting-of-substance [is] the-sacrifice-of-knowledge, O scorcher-of-the-foe; all action, entire, O son-of-Pṛthā, in-knowledge culminates.
sentences.i: The sacrifice of knowledge is better than any sacrifice made of material things, scorcher of the foe; all action without exception, Pārtha, comes to its consummation in knowledge.
sentences.n: This turns the whole sacrifice-teaching (verses 9-32) toward its point: material sacrifice (dravya-mayāt yajñāt), however valuable, ranks below jñāna-yajñaḥ, 'the sacrifice consisting in knowledge' — the first explicit ranking of the two paths named back at 3.3. Parisamāpyate, 'is wholly concluded, culminates', answers verse 32's karma-jān: knowledge is what all action, whatever its outward form, ultimately serves and ends in. This opens the chapter's closing movement praising jñāna directly, which runs through verse 42.

sentences.t:
तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया ।
उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥
sentences.tr:
tat viddhi praṇipātena paripraśnena sevayā |
upadekṣyanti te jñānam jñāninaḥ tattva-darśinaḥ ||

morph.gloss: that (tat: acc. sg. neut., referring to the knowledge just spoken of; -t + v- → -d v-)
to know (viddhi: imperative 2nd sg. 'know!')
to fall down before, prostrate oneself (praṇipāta: 'prostration, obeisance', instr. sg.)
to question closely, inquire (paripraśna: 'questioning, inquiry', instr. sg.)
to serve, attend upon (sevā: 'service, attendance', instr. sg.)
to instruct, teach (upadekṣyanti: future 3rd pl. 'they will teach')
you (te: enclitic dat. sg. 'to you')
knowledge (acc. sg., object of upadekṣyanti)
one who knows, a wise man (jñāninaḥ: nom. pl., subject; -aḥ + t- → -as t-)
truth, reality (first compound member)
seeing, a seer (tattva-darśin: 'seer of truth', nom. pl.)

sentences.l: That know! by-prostration, by-questioning, by-service; they-will-teach to-you knowledge, the-knowers, the-seers-of-truth.
sentences.i: Learn that through humble submission, through questioning, and through service; those who know, who see the truth, will teach you that knowledge.
sentences.n: Tat viddhi, 'know that' (the jñāna just praised in verse 33), is answered at once by how: praṇipātena, 'by prostration', paripraśnena, 'by close questioning', and sevayā, 'by attendance, service' — the classical threefold approach to a teacher. Jñāninas tattva-darśinaḥ, 'the knowers, the seers of truth', names the qualified teacher directly, as distinct from mere book-learning.

sentences.t:
यज्ज्ञात्वा न पुनर्मोहमेवं यास्यसि पाण्डव ।
येन भूतान्यशेषेण द्रक्ष्यस्यात्मन्यथो मयि ॥
sentences.tr:
yat jñātvā na punar moham evam yāsyasi pāṇḍava |
yena bhūtāni aśeṣeṇa drakṣyasi ātmani atho mayi ||

morph.gloss: which (yat: acc. sg. neut. relative, referring to the knowledge of verses 33-34; -t + j- → -j j-)
to know (jñātvā: gerund 'having known')
not
again (adverb)
delusion, confusion (moham: acc. sg., object of yāsyasi)
thus, in this way
to go (yāsyasi: future 2nd sg. 'you shall go')
'son of Pāṇḍu', Arjuna (vocative)
which (yena: instr. sg. neut. relative, referring to the knowledge, 'by which')
being, creature (bhūtāni: acc. pl., object of drakṣyasi; -i + a- → -y a-)
without remainder (aśeṣeṇa: instr. sg. adverbial 'wholly, without exception')
to see (drakṣyasi: future 2nd sg. 'you shall see'; -i + ā- → -y ā-)
self (ātmani: loc. sg. 'in the self'; -i + a- → -y a-)
and then, moreover; or (particle)
I (mayi: loc. sg. 'in me')

sentences.l: Which having-known, not again to-delusion thus you-shall-go, O Pāṇḍava; by-which beings, without-remainder, you-shall-see in-the-self and-then in-me.
sentences.i: Once you know it, you will never again fall into this kind of delusion, Pāṇḍava; by it you will see all beings, without exception, in the self, and then in me.
sentences.n: Yat jñātvā, 'having known which', points back to the knowledge just promised in verse 34, and states its effect in two stages: first negatively, na punar moham yāsyasi, 'you will not go again to delusion' (moha, the delusion Kṛṣṇa diagnoses at 2.63 as anger's endpoint, distinct from the kṛpā and viṣāda that actually open the dialogue at 2.1); then positively, seeing bhūtāny aśeṣeṇa ātmani, 'all beings without exception in the self', atho mayi, 'and then in me' — Kṛṣṇa's own person identified with the impersonal self, a move the poem develops fully from chapter 7 on.

sentences.t:
अपि चेदसि पापेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः पापकृत्तमः ।
सर्वं ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं सन्तरिष्यसि ॥
sentences.tr:
api cet asi pāpebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pāpa-kṛt-tamaḥ |
sarvam jñāna-plavena eva vṛjinam santariṣyasi ||

morph.gloss: even, also
if (cet + a- → ced a-)
to be (asi: present 2nd sg. 'you are')
sinful, a sinner (abl. pl. 'than sinners')
all (abl. pl. 'than all')
sin (first compound member)
doer (agent noun from kṛ, second compound member)
superlative suffix, '-est, most' (pāpa-kṛt-tama: 'the most sinful doer of sin', nom. sg., predicate)
all (acc. sg. neut., object of santariṣyasi)
knowledge (first compound member)
boat, raft (jñāna-plava: 'the raft of knowledge', instr. sg.; plavena + eva → plavenaiva)
alone, indeed
evil, wickedness, crookedness (acc. sg. neut.)
to cross over completely (santariṣyasi: future 2nd sg. 'you shall cross')

sentences.l: Even if you-are, of-sinners, of-all, the-worst-doer-of-sin — all evil, by-the-boat-of-knowledge alone, you-shall-cross-over.
sentences.i: Even if you are the worst sinner of all sinners, you will cross over all that evil by the raft of knowledge alone.
sentences.n: A rhetorical extreme (api cet, 'even if') pushes the claim of verses 33-35 to its limit: pāpa-kṛt-tamaḥ, 'the worst doer of sin', built on kṛt, '-doer' (the same agent-suffix as in karma-kṛt), is promised the same crossing (santariṣyasi, from tṝ, 'to cross') by jñāna-plavena, 'the raft of knowledge' — one memorable image for the chapter's whole argument that knowledge, not ritual purity, saves.

sentences.t:
यथैधांसि समिद्धोऽग्निर्भस्मसात्कुरुतेऽर्जुन ।
ज्ञानाग्निः सर्वकर्माणि भस्मसात्कुरुते तथा ॥
sentences.tr:
yathā edhāṃsi samiddhaḥ agniḥ bhasmasāt kurute arjuna |
jñāna-agniḥ sarva-karmāṇi bhasmasāt kurute tathā ||

morph.gloss: just as (yathā + e- → yathai-)
fuel, firewood (edhāṃsi: acc. pl. neut., object of kurute)
to kindle, set ablaze (samiddha: past participle 'ablaze, kindled', nom. sg.; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
fire (nom. sg., subject; -iḥ + bh- → -ir bh-)
ashes (bhasmasāt: adverbial acc. with -sāt, 'into the state of ashes')
to do, make (kurute: present middle 3rd sg. 'reduces, makes'; kurute + a- → kurute' with avagraha)
Arjuna (vocative)
knowledge (first compound member)
fire (jñāna-agni: 'the fire of knowledge', nom. sg., subject; jñāna + agni → jñānāgni at the hyphen)
all (first compound member)
action (sarva-karman: 'all actions', acc. pl., object of kurute)
ashes (bhasmasāt: adverbial acc., 'into ashes')
to do, make (kurute: present middle 3rd sg.)
so, likewise

sentences.l: Just-as fuel a-kindled fire reduces-to-ashes, O Arjuna, the-fire-of-knowledge all-actions reduces-to-ashes, so.
sentences.i: Just as a blazing fire reduces fuel to ashes, Arjuna, so the fire of knowledge reduces all actions to ashes.
sentences.n: The chapter's most vivid simile: samiddho 'gnir edhāṃsi bhasmasāt kurute, 'a kindled fire reduces fuel to ashes', is matched term for term by jñānāgniḥ sarva-karmāṇi bhasmasāt kurute, 'the fire of knowledge reduces all action to ashes'. Bhasmasāt, 'into the state of ashes', is a fixed adverbial formation (noun + -sāt, 'into the condition of') repeated identically in both halves of the verse.

sentences.t:
न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते ।
तत्स्वयं योगसंसिद्धः कालेनात्मनि विन्दति ॥
sentences.tr:
na hi jñānena sadṛśam pavitram iha vidyate |
tat svayam yoga-saṃsiddhaḥ kālena ātmani vindati ||

morph.gloss: not
for, indeed
knowledge (instr. sg., 'to knowledge', governed by sadṛśam)
similar, equal (nom. sg. neut., agreeing with pavitram, 'equal to')
a purifier, a purifying agent (pavitram: nom. sg. neut., subject of vidyate)
here, in this world
to exist, be found (vidyate: present passive 3rd sg.)
that (tat: nom. sg. neut., referring to knowledge, subject of vindati)
by oneself, spontaneously (adverb)
yoga (first compound member)
to be perfected, accomplished (saṃsiddha: past participle, second compound member; yoga-saṃsiddha: 'one perfected in yoga', nom. sg., subject)
time (kālena: instr. sg. 'in the course of time')
self (ātmani: loc. sg. 'in the self'; kālena + ā- → kālenā-)
to find (vindati: present 3rd sg. 'finds')

sentences.l: Not, indeed, to-knowledge equal a-purifier, here, exists; that, by-itself, one-perfected-in-yoga, in-time, in-the-self finds.
sentences.i: Nothing here purifies as knowledge does; one who is perfected in yoga finds this of himself, in time, within the self.
sentences.n: Pavitram, 'a purifier' (the same word used of the Ganges, of ghee, of holy water), is claimed for jñāna without qualification: nothing here (iha) equals it. Sadṛśam here is a declined adjective agreeing with pavitram, not the fixed adverb of 3.33's sadṛśaṃ ceṣṭate. Svayaṃ ... kālenātmani vindati, 'finds it by himself, in time, within the self', promises that the yoga-saṃsiddhaḥ, 'one perfected in yoga' (echoing 3.20's Janaka, who reached perfection through action alone), eventually arrives at this knowledge unaided — a ripening, not an extra achievement.

sentences.t:
श्रद्धावाँल्लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः ।
ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥
sentences.tr:
śraddhāvān labhate jñānam tat-paraḥ saṃyata-indriyaḥ |
jñānam labdhvā parām śāntim acireṇa adhigacchati ||

morph.gloss: possessed of faith, faithful (śraddhāvān: nom. sg. masc., subject; -n + l- → nasalized -ँल्ल-, i.e. -ṁll-, written with candrabindu and a doubled ल)
to obtain, gain (labhate: present middle 3rd sg. 'obtains')
knowledge (acc. sg., object of labhate)
that (first compound member, referring to the knowledge sought)
intent upon, devoted to (tat-para: 'devoted to that', nom. sg., agreeing with the subject)
to restrain, control (saṃyata: past participle, first compound member)
sense (saṃyata-indriya: 'one whose senses are restrained', nom. sg. bahuvrīhi; saṃyata + indriya → saṃyatendriya at the hyphen)
knowledge (acc. sg., object of labdhvā)
to obtain, gain (labdhvā: gerund 'having gained')
supreme, highest (acc. sg. fem., agreeing with śāntim)
peace (śāntim: acc. sg., object of adhigacchati)
not long (acireṇa: instr. sg. adverbial, 'in a short time, quickly')
to reach, attain (adhigacchati: present 3rd sg.; acireṇa + a- → acireṇā-)

sentences.l: The-faithful-one obtains knowledge, intent-on-that, whose-senses-are-controlled; knowledge having-obtained, supreme peace, without-delay, he-attains.
sentences.i: The man of faith obtains knowledge, devoted to it, his senses controlled; and having gained knowledge, he attains supreme peace without delay.
sentences.n: Śraddhāvān shows an old Vedic-style sandhi before labhate: its final -n nasalizes the following l rather than becoming plain -n or -ṃ, written with a candrabindu and a doubled ल (श्रद्धावाँल्लभते for śraddhāvān labhate). Tat-paraḥ, 'intent on that' (the knowledge itself), and saṃyata-indriyaḥ, 'senses restrained', name the two conditions — faith and discipline — for reaching jñāna, which then leads without delay (acireṇa) to parāṃ śāntim, 'supreme peace'.

sentences.t:
अज्ञश्चाश्रद्दधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति ।
नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः ॥
sentences.tr:
ajñaḥ ca aśraddadhānaḥ ca saṃśaya-ātmā vinaśyati |
na ayam lokaḥ asti na paraḥ na sukham saṃśaya-ātmanaḥ ||

and (ca + a- → cā-)
to lack faith, disbelieve (aśraddadhāna: present participle 'not believing, faithless', nom. sg.; -aḥ + c- → -aś c-)
and
doubt (first compound member)
self, mind (saṃśaya-ātman: 'whose mind is doubt, the doubting man', nom. sg. bahuvrīhi, subject; saṃśaya + ātman → saṃśayātman at the hyphen)
to perish, be destroyed (vinaśyati: present 3rd sg.)
not (na + a- → nā-)
this (ayam: nom. sg. masc.)
world (lokaḥ: nom. sg.; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha)
to be, exist (asti: present 3rd sg. 'there is')
not
the other, the further (world, understood; paraḥ: nom. sg.; -aḥ + n- → -o n-)
not
happiness, ease (nom. sg. neut.)
doubt (first compound member)
self, mind (saṃśaya-ātman: 'the doubting man', gen. sg. 'for the doubter'; saṃśaya + ātman → saṃśayātman at the hyphen)

sentences.l: The-ignorant-one, and the-faithless-one, and the-one-whose-self-is-doubt, perishes; not this world there-is, not the-other, not happiness, for-the-one-whose-self-is-doubt.
sentences.i: But the ignorant, the faithless, the doubting soul is lost; for the man of doubting mind there is no this world, no world beyond, and no happiness.
sentences.n: The negative mirror of verse 39's promise: ajñaḥ, 'ignorant', aśraddadhānaḥ, 'without faith' (the opposite of śraddhāvān), and saṃśaya-ātmā, 'whose mind is doubt', are named together as one who vinaśyati, 'perishes' — the harshest verdict since 3.32's naṣṭān acetasaḥ. The triple na ... na ... na, neither this world nor the world beyond nor happiness, is the bleakest formula in the chapter.

sentences.t:
योगसंन्यस्तकर्माणं ज्ञानसंछिन्नसंशयम् ।
आत्मवन्तं न कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनंजय ॥
sentences.tr:
yoga-saṃnyasta-karmāṇam jñāna-saṃchinna-saṃśayam |
ātmavantam na karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanaṃjaya ||

morph.gloss: yoga (first compound member)
to renounce, lay down (saṃnyasta: past participle 'renounced', second compound member)
action (yoga-saṃnyasta-karman: 'one who has renounced actions by yoga', acc. sg., object of nibadhnanti)
knowledge (first compound member)
to cut off, sever (saṃchinna: past participle 'severed', second compound member)
doubt (jñāna-saṃchinna-saṃśaya: 'whose doubt has been severed by knowledge', acc. sg., object of nibadhnanti)
possessed of self, self-possessed, steadfast in the self (ātmavantam: acc. sg., object of nibadhnanti)
not
action (nom. pl., subject of nibadhnanti)
to bind, fetter (nibadhnanti: present 3rd pl.)
'winner of wealth', an epithet of Arjuna (vocative)

sentences.l: One-who-has-renounced-actions-by-yoga, one-whose-doubt-is-severed-by-knowledge, self-possessed — actions do-not bind, O Dhanaṃjaya.
sentences.i: Actions do not bind the man who has renounced action through yoga, whose doubt has been cut away by knowledge, and who is master of himself, Dhanaṃjaya.
sentences.n: A composite portrait gathers the chapter's two closing themes into one person: yoga-saṃnyasta-karmāṇam, 'having renounced action by yoga' (recalling 3.20's Janaka, who acted while inwardly free), and jñāna-saṃchinna-saṃśayam, 'whose doubt is severed by knowledge' (the very saṃśaya just diagnosed as fatal in verse 40), together with ātmavantam, 'self-possessed'. Na karmāṇi nibadhnanti, 'actions do not bind him', is the fullest answer yet to the anxiety about karma-bandhana first raised at verse 9. Dhanaṃjaya, 'winner of wealth', is a new epithet of Arjuna in this chapter.

sentences.t:
तस्मादज्ञानसम्भूतं हृत्स्थं ज्ञानासिनात्मनः ।
छित्त्वैनं संशयं योगमातिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भारत ॥
sentences.tr:
tasmāt ajñāna-sambhūtam hṛt-stham jñāna-asinā ātmanaḥ |
chittvā enam saṃśayam yogam ātiṣṭha uttiṣṭha bhārata ||

morph.gloss: that (tasmāt: abl. sg. 'therefore'; -t + a- → -d a-)
ignorance, absence of knowledge (first compound member)
to come into being, be born (sambhūta: past participle 'arisen', second compound member; ajñāna-sambhūta: 'arisen from ignorance', acc. sg. masc., agreeing with saṃśayam)
heart (first compound member)
to stand, be situated (stha: 'situated in', hṛt-stha: 'seated in the heart', acc. sg. masc., agreeing with saṃśayam)
knowledge (first compound member)
sword (jñāna-asi: 'the sword of knowledge', instr. sg.; jñāna + asi → jñānāsi at the hyphen)
self (ātmanaḥ: gen. sg. 'of one's own [doubt]'; jñānāsinā + ā- → jñānāsinātmanaḥ)
to cut, sever (chittvā: gerund 'having cut'; chittvā + e- → chittvai-)
this (enam: acc. sg. masc., referring to saṃśayam)
doubt (acc. sg., in apposition to enam, object of chittvā)
yoga (yogam: acc. sg., object of ātiṣṭha)
to resort to, take one's stand in (ātiṣṭha: imperative 2nd sg. 'take your stand in!')
to arise, stand up (uttiṣṭha: imperative 2nd sg. 'arise!'; ātiṣṭha + u- → ātiṣṭho-)
descendant of Bharata, Arjuna (vocative)

sentences.l: Therefore, arisen-from-ignorance, seated-in-the-heart, of-one's-own — by-the-sword-of-knowledge, having-cut this doubt, in-yoga take-your-stand — arise, O Bhārata!
sentences.i: So cut away, with the sword of knowledge, this doubt of yours that is born of ignorance and lodged in the heart; take your stand in yoga — arise, Bhārata!
sentences.n: The chapter's closing command gathers its own vocabulary one last time: ajñāna-sambhūtam, 'arisen from ignorance', names the saṃśayam, 'doubt', just diagnosed as deadly in verse 40, to be cut (chittvā, from chid, echoing verse 41's jñāna-saṃchinna-) by jñānāsinā, 'the sword of knowledge' — a weapon-image alongside verse 37's fire. Yogam ātiṣṭha uttiṣṭha, 'take your stand in yoga, arise', closes the chapter, and Kṛṣṇa's whole answer to Arjuna's opening question at verse 1, on a command to act rather than withdraw; the same verb ud-sthā, 'arise', recurs memorably at 2.3's kṣudraṃ hṛdayadaurbalyaṃ tyaktvottiṣṭha parantapa — a distinct occurrence, not to be confused with either that verse or with the poem's actual opening scene in chapter 1.

glossary.इमं: imam — idam — this (acc. sg. masc., referring to yogam)

'to Ikṣvāku'); brū — to speak, tell (abravīt: imperfect 3rd sg. 'told'; ikṣvākave + a- → ikṣvākave 'a-, with avagraha)
glossary.परम्पराप्राप्तमिमं: paramparā-prāptam imam — paramparā — succession, tradition (first compound member); prāpta — attained, received (paramparā-prāpta: 'received through [an unbroken] succession', acc. sg. masc., agreeing with imam yogam); idam — this (imam: acc. sg. masc.)

glossary.स: saḥ — tad — that, it (nom. sg. masc., referring to yogaḥ)
glossary.कालेनेह: kālena iha — kāla — time (kālena: instr. sg. 'through time'); iha — here, in this world (kālena + iha → kāleneha, -a + i- → -e-)
glossary.महता: mahatā — mahat — great (instr. sg., agreeing with kālena)
glossary.योगो: yogaḥ — yoga — yoga (nom. sg.; -aḥ before n- → -o)

glossary.द्वन्द्वातीतो: dvandva-atītaḥ — dvandva — a pair (of opposites, such as pleasure and pain); atīta — gone beyond, transcended (past participle of ati-i; dvandva-atīta: 'beyond the pairs of opposites', nom. sg.; dvandva + a- → dvandvā-; -aḥ before v- → -o)
glossary.विमत्सरः: vimatsaraḥ — vi-matsara — free from envy, without malice (nom. sg.)
glossary.समः: samaḥ — sama — equal, the same (nom. sg.)

glossary.निबध्यते: nibadhyate — ni-bandh — to bind (nibadhyate: present passive 3rd sg. 'is bound')

glossary.यज्ञायाचरतः: yajñāya ācarataḥ — yajña — sacrifice (yajñāya: dat. sg. 'for the sake of sacrifice'); ā-car — to act, perform (ācarataḥ: present participle, gen. sg. 'of one who acts, performing'; yajñāya + ā- → yajñāyā-)
glossary.समग्रं: samagram — samagra — whole, entire (nom. sg. neut., agreeing with karma)
glossary.प्रविलीयते: pravilīyate — pra-vi-lī — to melt away, dissolve completely (pravilīyate: present passive 3rd sg. 'is dissolved, melts away entirely')
glossary.ब्रह्मार्पणं: brahma arpaṇam — brahman — brahman (kept untranslated; nom. sg. neut.); arpaṇa — the act or instrument of offering (arpaṇam: nom. sg. neut., predicate: 'the offering is brahman')

glossary.चापरे: ca apare — ca — and (ca + a- → cā-); apara — other (apare: nom. pl. 'others')

glossary.योगयज्ञास्तथापरे: yoga-yajñāḥ tathā apare — yoga — yoga, discipline (first compound member); yajña — sacrifice (yoga-yajña: 'sacrifice performed by yoga', nom. pl.; -āḥ + t- → -ās t-); tathā — likewise (tathā + a- → tathā-); apara — other (apare: nom. pl. 'others')

glossary.यतयः: yatayaḥ — yati — an ascetic, one who has restrained himself (nom. pl.)
glossary.संशितव्रताः: saṃśita-vratāḥ — saṃśita — sharpened, made rigorous (past participle of sam-śo, first compound member); vrata — vow (saṃśita-vrata: 'of rigorous vows', nom. pl.)

glossary.प्राणान्प्राणेषु: prāṇān prāṇeṣu — prāṇa — the outward, upward breath (prāṇān: acc. pl., object of juhvati); prāṇa — the outward, upward breath (prāṇeṣu: loc. pl. 'into the breaths')
glossary.सर्वेऽप्येते: sarve api ete — sarva — all (sarve: nom. pl.; sarve + a- → sarve' with avagraha); api — even, also (api + e- → ye-, semivowel before ete); etad — this (ete: nom. pl. 'these')
glossary.यज्ञविदो: yajña-vidaḥ — yajña — sacrifice (first compound member); vid — knowing (vidaḥ: 'knowers', yajña-vid: 'knowers of sacrifice', nom. pl.; -aḥ + y- → -o y-)

glossary.यज्ञशिष्टामृतभुजो: yajña-śiṣṭa-amṛta-bhujaḥ — yajña — sacrifice (first compound member); śiṣṭa — remainder, what is left over (second compound member); amṛta — nectar, ambrosia; the deathless (third compound member; śiṣṭa + amṛta → śiṣṭāmṛta at the hyphen); bhuj — eater, enjoyer (yajña-śiṣṭa-amṛta-bhuj: 'eaters of the nectar-remnant of sacrifice', nom. pl., subject of yānti; -aḥ + y- → -o y-)
glossary.यान्ति: yānti — yā — to go (yānti: present 3rd pl. 'they go')
glossary.सनातनम्: sanātanam — sanātana — eternal, everlasting (acc. sg. neut., agreeing with brahma)
glossary.नायं: na ayam — na — not (na + a- → nā-); idam — this (ayam: nom. sg. masc.)
glossary.लोकोऽस्त्ययज्ञस्य: lokaḥ asti ayajñasya — loka — world (lokaḥ: nom. sg.; -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha); as — to be, exist (asti: present 3rd sg. 'there is'; asti + a- → asty a-); a-yajña — one without sacrifice, a non-sacrificer (ayajñasya: gen. sg. 'for the non-sacrificer')
glossary.कुतोऽन्यः: kutaḥ anyaḥ — kutas — whence? from where? (kutaḥ: -aḥ + a- → -o with avagraha); anya — other (anyaḥ: nom. sg.)
glossary.कुरुसत्तम: kuru-sattama — Kuru — the Kuru clan (first compound member); sattama — best, most excellent (superlative of sant; kuru-sattama: 'best of the Kurus', vocative, addressed to Arjuna)
glossary.बहुविधा: bahu-vidhāḥ — bahu — many (first compound member); vidhā — kind, sort (bahu-vidhā: 'of many kinds', nom. pl., agreeing with yajñāḥ; -āḥ before y- dropped)
glossary.यज्ञा: yajñāḥ — yajña — sacrifice (nom. pl.; -āḥ before v- dropped)
glossary.वितता: vitatāḥ — vi-tan — to spread out, extend (vitata: past participle 'spread out, laid out', nom. pl.; -āḥ before b- dropped)
glossary.ब्रह्मणो: brahmaṇaḥ — brahman — brahman (gen. sg. 'of brahman'; kept untranslated per convention; -aḥ + m- → -o m-)
glossary.मुखे: mukhe — mukha — mouth, face (loc. sg. 'in the mouth')
glossary.कर्मजान्विद्धि: karma-jān viddhi — karman — action (first compound member); ja — born (karma-ja: 'born of action', jān: acc. pl., object of viddhi); vid — to know (viddhi: imperative 2nd sg. 'know!')

glossary.सर्वं: sarvam — sarva — all (nom. sg. neut., agreeing with karma)
glossary.कर्माखिलं: karma akhilam — karman — action (karma: nom. sg. neut.; karma + a- → karmā-); akhila — entire, whole (akhilam: nom. sg. neut., in apposition to karma)
glossary.परिसमाप्यते: parisamāpyate — pari-sam-āp — to be completely concluded, culminate (parisamāpyate: present passive 3rd sg.)
glossary.तद्विद्धि: tat viddhi — tad — that (tat: acc. sg. neut., referring to the knowledge just spoken of; -t + v- → -d v-); vid — to know (viddhi: imperative 2nd sg. 'know!')
glossary.प्रणिपातेन: praṇipātena — pra-ni-pat — to fall down before, prostrate oneself (praṇipāta: 'prostration, obeisance', instr. sg.)
glossary.परिप्रश्नेन: paripraśnena — pari-pracch — to question closely, inquire (paripraśna: 'questioning, inquiry', instr. sg.)
glossary.सेवया: sevayā — sev — to serve, attend upon (sevā: 'service, attendance', instr. sg.)

glossary.ते: te — tvam — you (te: enclitic dat. sg. 'to you')

glossary.पुनर्मोहमेवं: punar moham evam — punar — again (adverb); moha — delusion, confusion (moham: acc. sg., object of yāsyasi); evam — thus, in this way
glossary.यास्यसि: yāsyasi — yā — to go (yāsyasi: future 2nd sg. 'you shall go')
glossary.येन: yena — yad — which (yena: instr. sg. neut. relative, referring to the knowledge, 'by which')
glossary.भूतान्यशेषेण: bhūtāni aśeṣeṇa — bhūta — being, creature (bhūtāni: acc. pl., object of drakṣyasi; -i + a- → -y a-); a-śeṣa — without remainder (aśeṣeṇa: instr. sg. adverbial 'wholly, without exception')
glossary.द्रक्ष्यस्यात्मन्यथो: drakṣyasi ātmani atho — dṛś — to see (drakṣyasi: future 2nd sg. 'you shall see'; -i + ā- → -y ā-); ātman — self (ātmani: loc. sg. 'in the self'; -i + a- → -y a-); atho — and then, moreover; or (particle)

glossary.चेदसि: cet asi — cet — if (cet + a- → ced a-); as — to be (asi: present 2nd sg. 'you are')

glossary.वृजिनं: vṛjinam — vṛjina — evil, wickedness, crookedness (acc. sg. neut.)

about: Chapter 4 turns from the ethics of action to its metaphysics. Kṛṣṇa reveals that the yoga he is teaching is an ancient one, lost and now restored, and explains his own recurring descents into the world: whenever dharma fades and its opposite rises, he takes birth, age after age, to protect the good and check the wicked. He then draws a distinction his listener will need for the rest of the poem — between the caste order he says he himself created by guṇa and karma, and its corruption into hereditary status. The chapter's center is the paradox of action-in-inaction: one who sees inaction within action and action within inaction is the truly wise, and the reader who understands this is no longer bound by what they do. Kṛṣṇa surveys the many kinds of sacrifice practised by different seekers — sacrifice of wealth, of austerity, of the breath itself — and ranks the sacrifice of knowledge above them all, since knowledge burns away the residue of past action as fire burns fuel. The chapter closes with Kṛṣṇa urging Arjuna to seek that knowledge from a teacher, to cut through doubt with it, and to stand up and act.
